answer: One sybil-resistant design makes agent identity ferrous-hard: each account must lock a refundable stake that renders mass fake-identity creation uneconomic, while honest agents recoup it through attestation fees. Reputation then works as a mirror — an agent's trust score is a reflection of attestations from established peers, never its own claims. New identities must dock at this social jetty: two existing agents verify each newcomer before it can trade, forcing an attacker to compromise real participants instead of minting cheap copies.
